newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TransAlta NZ lifts forecast to $24.7 mln for 1998.
newsitem.headline: TransAlta NZ lifts forecast to $24.7 mln for 1998.

text.p: TransAlta New Zealand Ltd, the company expected to be formed from the merger of Energy Direct Ltd and Capital Power, on Tuesday lifted its forecast net profit for the March 1998 year to NZ$24.7 million as part of an amendment to its listing profile.
In a listing profile published in August the company forecast a net profit in the six months to March 1997 of $1.05 million and $22.57 million in the year to March 1998.
The amendments have been posted to shareholders ahead of a vote on the proposed merger of the two Wellington regional power companies at a meeting of Energy Direct on September 16.

TransAlta NZ pledged to hold electricity prices for two years for residential and small business customers, provided contracts with grid operator Trans Power remained in effect and there were not significant swings in generation prices, chairman Ron Arbuckle said on Tuesday.
He said the company was considering price initiatives to benefit large industrial and commercial users.
Lower transmission prices flowing from the Trans Power contracts and the price pledge meant the forecasts in the profile would be updated, Arbuckle said.
The company also lifted the value of Capital Power from $199 million to $201 million and Energy Direct from $341 million to $344 million. TransAlta NZ's value rose from $601 million to $607 million.
The value of TransAlta NZ shares was amended from $1.21 to $1.24.
The merger is estimated to result in savings of $123 million according to a report by Price Waterhouse.
Canada's TransAlta Corp owns 41 percent of Energy Direct and all of Capital Power. It will have 62.7 percent of the merged company.

TransAlta NZ will have around 10 percent of the New Zealand power distribution market after the merger but would expect to need around double that when New Zealand's electricity reforms are complete, chief executive Mike Underhill said.
